page: Amazon Web Services x8g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core and memory performance. The x8g.24xlarge achieves top-decile results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Its memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 480.45 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 215.69 GB/sec. Database and in-memory operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by top-tier Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reach 193.44 million operations per second. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests.

Given its massive memory capacity and high multi-core throughput, the x8g.24xlarge is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that scale horizontally across ARM64 architectures. The absence of local storage means it relies on network-attached storage, making it best suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing. It also shows strong capability in executing medium and large language model text generation, where it achieves top-tier inference speeds.
